intent: Recover a TachiyomiSY library destroyed by a silent partial restore, and add a guard so a collapsed sync payload can never again become the only copy.
scope: python_pkg/syncyomi_guard/ — new package: protobuf payload decoder, collapse detection, snapshot store, CLI
docs/syncyomi-restore-runbook.md — restore procedure and WAL recovery steps
Non-goal: fixing the upstream bug. It is Kotlin in a third-party APK (jobobby04/TachiyomiSY#1634, #1638, both open). The guard detects and preserves; it cannot prevent.
changes: Diagnosed the failure as phone-side, not server-side: android.database.SQLException code 5 in BackupRestoreJob via Room InvalidationTracker. Server logged zero errors and PRAGMA quick_check returned ok.
Recovered the pre-damage 14 MB payload by replaying all 3447 WAL frames over the base database (last writer wins) and extracting sync_data.data; wrote it out as a gzipped .tachibk.

Deliberately did NOT checkpoint the WAL when first asked: it held the only surviving copy of the library. Deferred until after recovery, then done via a graceful container restart (14201672 -> 0 bytes).

payload.py: dependency-free Backup protobuf reader counting manga (field 1), categories (field 2), chapters (field 16, nested) and sources (field 101); rejects trailing bytes so splice damage cannot decode as success.
verdict.py: fails on >10% drop or a fall to zero in manga, chapters or categories; a missing baseline reports FIRST_RUN rather than a pass.
store.py: reads the live database through an immutable URI (never locks it, never triggers the SQLITE_BUSY class of failure it detects) and keeps N restorable .tachibk snapshots.
Prune glob tightened to the timestamp shape so a hand-named recovery file cannot be deleted as a stale snapshot.

verification.command: protoc --decode_raw < payload.bin | grep -cE '^1 \{'  (independent cross-check of the hand-written decoder)
verification.evidence: protoc and python_pkg.syncyomi_guard agree exactly on all three real payloads: recovered 2182 manga / 18 categories, stub 0 / 0, post-restore 2182 / 0.

verification.command: python3 -m python_pkg.syncyomi_guard --db <db holding the real 267KB stub> --state-dir <real baseline>
verification.evidence: COLLAPSED: manga went from 2182 to 0; chapters went from 68418 to 0. EXIT=1, no snapshot written. Replays the actual 22:53 incident end to end through the binary.
ok: 2182 manga, 68418 chapters, 0 categories, 24 sources (12277887 bytes); snapshot written. Ran against the live database while the container was serving.
status=0/SUCCESS in the real deploy environment; journal shows the ok line and the snapshot path.
59 passed; 100% branch coverage across all five modules.

verification.command: distinct chapter URL comparison, recovered backup vs post-restore server payload
verification.evidence: Both sides 57389 distinct chapters. The 75376 -> 68418 fall was 6958 intra-manga duplicates being collapsed, not data loss. Prevented a false 'chapters lost' report and a wrongly tightened threshold.

risks: Categories are NOT recovered: 18 definitions and 1724 manga-to-category assignments were lost and only exist in syncyomi_recovered_2026-08-09.tachibk. Restoring them needs another full restore, which is another roll of the code-5 dice.
The current baseline records categories=0, and _drop_reason returns None when previous == 0, so category loss stays invisible until a healthy run raises the baseline above zero.
The guard reads the payload SyncYomi stores; it cannot see a phone-side library that has not yet synced.
The 10% threshold is calibrated to one incident. A slow drip below 10% per run would not trip it.
rollback: Delete python_pkg/syncyomi_guard/ — nothing else imports it.

Library recovery is independent of the guard: ~/syncyomi/recovery/syncyomi_recovered_2026-08-09.tachibk (sha256 cf00bee4b449255716387efe0587045f7b0b92a6c54327dd9dd3cfc7746ed7c3) restores 2182 manga, 75376 chapter entries and 18 categories.
After rollback, verify the server payload still decodes to 2182 manga.
